Chapter 128: First Update (Part 1)

A piece of news quickly swept across the entire world—an academy had been established with no restrictions on background or status. As long as one could pass the entrance examination, anyone could enroll and study free of charge.

The larger nations had long maintained their own academies, which admitted nobles and a tiny fraction of exceptionally gifted commoners. Without exception, these institutions focused solely on teaching methods to raise combat power.

This new, open-to-all academy was fundamentally different. The scope of knowledge it offered was so vast that it left people astonished: *Can things like this be taught in an academy?*

It bore no formal title and was simply referred to as the "Nameless Academy." Upon entering, students spent their first year collectively studying basic foundational disciplines encompassing all fields. After one year, they were divided into specialized branches based on their personal preferences and academic performance.

Within the academy, from politics and economics at the high end down to agriculture and craftsmanship at the low, anything you wished to learn—provided you passed the requisite exams—could be studied free of charge. Students who achieved outstanding academic results, completed assignments set by the academy, or passed trials arranged by their mentors could even earn rare resources virtually unobtainable in the outside world. Not to mention, it opened up the possibility of gaining recognition before major powers and securing a brilliant future.

Some nobles voiced skepticism, while others questioned whether the academy aligned with the holy doctrines of the God of Light, suspecting a secret connection to the God of Darkness behind the scenes.

It was later proven that the academy indeed shared a connection with the God of Darkness—it soon opened a branch in the Demon Realm, complete with a teleportation array linking the two campuses.

Although both the Holy Temple of Light and the Temple of Darkness claimed total ignorance, with the Pope displaying a thoroughly "shocked" expression, both campuses were situated in the sacred lands of Light and Darkness respectively. Furthermore, the teaching staff consisted entirely of young powerhouses from the churches who adamantly refused to admit they belonged to the churches. The nobility of various nations gradually caught on to the subtle reality. Could this academy be operating under the tacit authorization of both the God of Light and the God of Darkness?

Nobles were educated in history. Digging through ancient records, they learned that the War of Light and Darkness had not originally been a localized conflict involving only a Hero and a Demon King, as it was now, but rather a true, endless world war that had enveloped the entire globe in flames.

It seemed the God of Light and the God of Darkness had reached some sort of agreement, unwilling to let the finest talents of both races be consumed every century in the fires of war. Thus, they had staged a perfunctory conflict—termed a "war," but in truth a mere competition known as the "Great War of Light and Darkness."

Thereafter, the number of elite prodigies in both races surged. Young powerhouses sprang up like mushrooms after rain, and prosperous towns and nations multiplied rapidly.

Though the God of Light and the God of Darkness were destined to be enemies due to their opposing elemental attributes, both truly cherished their respective people. Seeing that humans and demons had regained their vitality, it was hardly difficult to understand why the two deities would wish to impart greater knowledge, enabling both races to flourish even further.

The nobles were also aware that Light and Darkness were not the only two deities in existence. Perhaps an anonymous third deity had stepped forward to make the creation of this academy possible. Because imparting such knowledge would increase the strength of both races, it was necessary to remain completely impartial, establishing branches for both sides.

There were plenty of clever people in the world. With both Popes acting half-concealed and half-revealing, the sharp-witted soon took the bait. Without any need for public promotion, various kingdoms sent their own prodigies to try their luck while gathering further intelligence.

Yet regardless of whatever ulterior motives they originally harbored, once enrolled in this academy, any extraneous thoughts were thoroughly shattered.

For no other reason than this: studying was simply too difficult.

You look down on farming and crafting? Then do you know why the crops grow the way they do, or the underlying principles behind how materials aggregate when crafting objects?

Mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology—these are the bedrock of the world. If you know nothing of them, how do you expect to break through to the Legendary realm and ignite divine fire? Do you think gods are merely good at fighting?

Pay attention! The rules governing all things in existence are commanded by the gods. In other words, to become a god, one must master these rules. Did you think this academy was just teaching you how to till land and manufacture items? Wrong! What this academy teaches is the knowledge required to attain godhood!

What? You can't comprehend mathematics, physics, or chemistry?

No matter. If you don't understand the natural sciences, there are humanities as well.

The origins of human culture and civilization, the evolution of social structures, the fundamental logic of interpersonal relations... The business and political studies you nobles learned in the past were merely scratching the surface. Here, we look through the phenomena to see the essence!

And behind each of these essences stands a deity!

The students suddenly attained enlightenment.

So the force behind this academy truly was the great deities—They intended to nurture even more gods!

Whenever dizzy, lightheaded students gazed at the Library Tower—where books could be borrowed indefinitely so long as one possessed enough academic credits—their eyes filled with overwhelming awe and reverence.

In this world, books were exceedingly rare. Even noble academies only taught the most superficial, basic knowledge. If one wished to advance further, one had to formally pledge oneself to a master. Even royalty had to acknowledge several teachers to learn the specialized knowledge of the factions behind those masters. And even if one secured a master, top-tier spells were not guaranteed to be handed down. Secret manuals were closely guarded treasures that even blood relatives might never be allowed to lay eyes upon.

Yet in this Library Tower, as long as you were willing to learn, you could study anything.

Consequently, numerous Legendary Warriors and Legendary Mages had come seeking trouble for the academy.

However, after arriving to negotiate, they discovered that even the academy's cafeteria staff were Legendary powerhouses, causing their overbearing momentum to deflate by half.

*Pope of Light, Pope of Darkness—you still dare claim this academy has nothing to do with your churches? You've practically stuffed every Legendary powerhouse in existence in here! Do you take us for blind?!*

The Holy Church of Light and the Church of Darkness only directly governed their own papal states. As for affairs in the rest of the world, unless it pertained to the War of Light and Darkness, they refrained from interfering or proselytizing.

Every element in this world was tied to either Light or Darkness. Neither the God of Light nor the God of Darkness needed to spread faith; there were more than enough people who believed in Them naturally. Furthermore, having reached a level of power as grand as Theirs, faith offered no further boost to Their strength. Their love for humanity was born purely of benevolence.

Because the God of Light and the God of Darkness were deeply compassionate toward their subjects, even if they couldn't defeat the churches' Legendary powerhouses, other troublesome Legendary figures still sought to make unreasonable demands. Some even gathered groups of scholars and apprentices to cause a commotion at the Library Tower, claiming that the tower housed secret manuals belonging to their factions and demanding they be burned.

Just as their clamor reached a peak, someone began descending the steps from within the Library Tower. With every step that person took, the pressure inside the tower multiplied. By the time he reached the base, everyone except the Legendary powerhouses was pinned flat against the floor, entirely unable to move.

"Headmaster Qin." The academy teachers felt no pressure whatsoever. They bowed respectfully toward the newcomer.

Two years ago, they had harbored doubts and disdain for this young man. Today, nothing remained in their hearts but profound awe.

Qin Lang swept his gaze across the unruly Legendary Mage. The mage's breath hitched instantly; the shadow behind him lost its form, morphing into a writhing, chaotic mass of black darkness.

The Legendary Warriors and Mages with keen perception felt their hairs stand on end as every sense screamed a dire warning: *The person before us is dangerous—extremely dangerous! Get away immediately!*

"If you want to make a scene, take it outside. You're disturbing him," Qin Lang said, a faint crease forming between his brows, his tone thoroughly impatient. "If you can't resolve this yourselves, tell me, and I'll do it."

Qin Lang's gaze settled upon the Legendary Mage whose mind he had forcibly locked down. One second, two seconds... ten seconds. Only then did he release his restraint.

The Legendary Mage collapsed stiffly onto the ground.

He panted violently, sweat drenching his clothes in an instant. His face was filled with absolute terror, wheezing gasps issuing from his wide-open mouth, unable to utter a single coherent word.

"Get out," Qin Lang said indifferently.

The Legendary Mage scrambled frantically on all fours, crawling out of the tower without a shred of dignity remaining, leaving behind all the disciples and apprentices he had brought along.

"Apologies, we will handle this immediately." Seeing that Qin Lang had not dealt a lethal blow, Roland let out a sigh of relief. "It was our oversight to let these people disturb Headmaster Xia's meditation."

Having received Roland's assurance, Qin Lang turned and headed back toward the top of the tower.

The pressure at the base of the tower dissipated alongside his departure. Those pinned to the ground lay unconscious, blood oozing from the corners of their mouths.

A Legendary Demon warrior who had come to investigate—who was also the king of the largest Demon nation, as well as Roland's father—asked in a trembling voice, "Who was that?"

罗兰道：“我们的学院长。你该庆幸我主庇佑着你们，不让他随意杀掉很稀少的传说强者。”

罗兰心中震撼无比。

最初见到秦琅的时候，秦琅连铁刀都拿不动；他再次见到秦琅，秦琅已经晋升传说；学院第一次招生的时候，全学院的传说强者都打不过秦琅了。

如今再次见面，他怀疑秦琅已经是行走在地上的神灵。

神灵怎么能在保留实力的前提下在世间行走？世界不会排斥他吗？

“咯咯咯咯！”窗台处传来愉快的笑声。

罗兰往窗台一看，毛绒绒并且胖……大了好几圈的黑色小兽正对满地倒霉蛋捧腹大笑，另一只白色小兽慢吞吞地从窗台飞进来，往塔顶飞去。

我主和我主的敌人都没意见，大概是没问题吧。

秦琅震慑了那群来挑事的传说强者，罗兰很友好地将人请了出去。

他相信，从此后不会再有人敢来打学院的主意。

罗兰离开藏书塔的时候，目光眺望塔顶。

夏先生已经整整一年，完全没有离开过塔顶了。

……

秦琅回到塔顶。

塔顶从外面看着是完全用黑色的巨石封闭，从里往外看，却是四面透明的水晶窗。

丝绸窗帘从四周的窗户垂落，半遮住耀眼的阳光。

塔顶的穹顶也是透明的。上面有许多黑色的纹路，乍一眼看去，仿佛聚集了许多恶心的飞虫。

走近一看，那些黑色纹路居然全部是文字。

窸窸窣窣的声音从地面响起。文字从地面银色的波纹中涌出，沿着地面和墙壁如山洪般蔓延。它们就像是一个个小人，一边遍地乱跑四处乱爬，一边扭打。

缺胳膊少腿的文字被堆在了地上，重新融进了银色的波纹中；胜利的文字沿着墙壁攀爬，一直蔓延到了整个穹顶。文字们扭曲推攘抖动，发出让人捂住耳朵也能听见的尖细嚎叫声。

这些文字都是夏兮风鉴定的“知识”。

文字靠近穹顶中间的光团时，穹顶挤满的字迹被光芒融化成墨迹，被外神力量浸染的知识汇聚成了细小的泉流，注入了穹顶的光团中。

光团闪烁，一本书逐渐成形。

穿着一身宽松睡袍的夏兮风赤脚站在光团下，两眼无神。

他的脚下银波荡漾。

“吵闹的人被我丢出去了。”秦琅将夏兮风抱起来，垂头蹭了蹭夏兮风的发顶。

夏兮风虽然面无反应，双手却自然地环住了秦琅的脖子。

作者有话要说：

时隔一年例假来了，抱歉白天没更新，痛哭流涕。为补偿，今天还有一章加更，会比较晚，大家别等。

Chapter 128: First Update (Part 2)

Roland replied, "Our Headmaster. You should be grateful that our Lord protects you, preventing him from casually slaughtering the scarce Legendary powerhouses."

Roland's heart was filled with indescribable shock.

When he first met Qin Lang, the man couldn't even lift an iron blade. When he saw him again, Qin Lang had already advanced to the Legendary realm. By the time the academy held its very first student enrollment, not a single Legendary powerhouse in the entire academy combined could defeat Qin Lang.

Now, meeting him once more, Roland suspected that Qin Lang was already a god walking the mortal realm.

How could a deity walk among mortals while retaining such terrifying power? Wouldn't the world reject him?

"Giggle giggle giggle!" A merry burst of laughter sounded from the window sill.

Roland looked toward the window sill. A fluffy, fat... black little beast—having grown several sizes larger—was clutching its stomach, laughing hysterically at the fallen unfortunates scattered across the ground. Meanwhile, a white little beast flew lazily through the window, gliding up toward the top of the tower.

*Since both my Lord and my Lord's enemy have no objections, it's probably fine,* Roland thought.

Having intimidated the group of troublemaking Legendary figures through Qin Lang's overwhelming presence, Roland courteously escorted them off the premises.

He was certain that from this day forth, no one would ever dare harbor designs against the academy again.

As Roland departed from the Library Tower, he cast his gaze up toward the topmost floor.

Mr. Xia had not left the top of the tower for an entire year.

...

Qin Lang returned to the top floor.

From the outside, the top of the tower appeared completely sealed off by massive black stones. Yet looking outward from the inside, it revealed transparent crystal windows on all four sides.

Silk curtains hung draped around the windows, partially blocking out the glaring sunlight.

The ceiling at the top was also transparent. Carved across it were countless black runes that, at a casual glance, resembled a swarm of repulsive flying insects.

Upon closer inspection, those black markings proved to be written words.

A rustling sound echoed from the floor. Words gushed forth from silver ripples along the ground, spreading across the floor and walls like a raging mountain flood. They behaved like tiny living figures, running, crawling, and wrestling wildly with one another.

Mutilated, broken words piled up on the ground before dissolving back into the silver ripples, while the victorious characters scrambled up the walls until they covered the entire dome. The words twisted, shoved, and vibrated, producing a high-pitched, piercing screech that resonated even if one covered their ears.

All these words were "knowledge" identified and appraised by Xia Xifeng.

As the text neared the light orb at the center of the dome, the dense writing covering the ceiling was melted into ink by the divine glow. Knowledge tainted by the power of outer gods gathered into slender trickles, flowing directly into the sphere of light atop the ceiling.

The light orb flickered, and a book gradually materialized.

Clad in a loose nightrobe, Xia Xifeng stood barefoot beneath the orb of light, his eyes vacant and devoid of focus.

Silver waves surged beneath his feet.

"I threw the noisy intruders out," Qin Lang said as he lifted Xia Xifeng into his arms, lowering his head to nuzzle the crown of his hair.

Though Xia Xifeng showed no conscious reaction, his arms naturally folded around Qin Lang's neck.

***

第129章 二更

塔顶只看摆设，是一个再普通不过的卧室。

这里有书桌书架，有衣柜大床，地面本来铺着厚厚软软的地毯。现在地毯被银波覆盖，房间地板仿佛是银色的大海。

秦琅抱着夏兮风来到书桌前，桌面上放着厚厚一摞需要学院长亲自批改的文件。

他坐在椅子上批改文件，夏兮风抱着他的脖子坐在他的怀里，慢慢闭上了双眼，继续“沉睡”。

细小的触须从秦琅的影子中探出，轻轻簇拥着秦琅怀里的夏兮风。秦琅双手不护着夏兮风，夏兮风也能在他怀里安睡。

地面上的银波微微荡漾，有触须在银波中漂浮。触须沾染上银色，原本浑浊的颜色镀上了一层银辉，映得触须仿佛变成了半透明，深沉无光的触须多了几分流光溢彩。

白色小兽飞到顶楼房间，看见房间里的异象，眼中仍旧难掩惊异。

黑色小兽也飞了上来：“虽然我俩认可了夏和秦，但他们居然能在这个世界悄悄点燃神火，也太厉害了。”

白色小兽点头。

秦琅听见两只小兽的声音，背对着祂们扬了扬手中的文件，示意两只小兽可以把文件搬下去了。

使唤神灵投影，秦琅从来不手软。

两只搬运工小兽飞到书桌上，小短腿一伸坐好。

白色小兽担忧道：“夏这次沉睡的时间好长，都半年没醒了。半年前也就醒了几个小时。真的没问题吗？”

黑色小兽只关心祂的零食：“可恶的夏兮风已经半年没给我做点心啦！”

秦琅瞥了两只毛绒绒一眼，没回答。

夏兮风确实暂时没问题，但他心情很不好，不认为这算没问题。

建立学院，系统任务更新，鉴定技能本土化后，秦琅身上桎梏陡然一松，实力飞速攀升，很快就点燃神火，重回半神。

按照系统最初的说法，他和夏兮风是偷渡者，在这个世界不应该点燃神火，一定会止步传说。

但或许光明神和黑暗神与世界纠缠太深，确实成了世界意识的代言人。祂们承认了夏兮风，联手为夏兮风遮蔽神皇的注视，夏兮风和他便回到了应有的境界，成了这个世界的“外神”。

之后夏兮风和秦琅的实力不断攀升，神火越来越强，与这个世界的联系越来越深，实力几乎快与梦世界持平。

夏兮风不断用鉴定技能了解这个世界的事务，将知识录入系统，秦琅帮他整理后，让系统拷贝成书籍。

这时他们的生活还很正常，夏兮风每天只花费半日在录书上，剩下半天就去种地做东西教书，或者让又能用暗影传送（黑暗神开的权限）满世界乱逛的秦琅带他去旅游。

这个世界还很和平，强者不多，秦琅可以带着夏兮风满世界乱逛，玩的地方比在梦世界中还多。

每到一个地方，夏兮风就哐哐哐砸鉴定术，分析当地有哪些有价值的矿石和动植物，经过秦琅分类整理后，让系统形成图鉴。

旅行之后，夏兮风就回到学院，尝试用新发现的材料创造物品。

等他能熟练运用新的材料后，就让系统录书，藏书塔便多了一本收藏。

出门旅游，回家完善图鉴，顺带逗一逗学生，给学生的考试增加难度……最初秦琅挺喜欢这样的生活。

虽然这个世界也有末日危机，但末日已经注定，做任何事都是无谓的挣扎，既然无所谓结果，他们每天过得都很轻松。

除了两只毛绒绒老是打扰他和夏兮风的二人生活，秦琅对在这个世界的生活，比梦世界还满意几分。

梦世界让夏兮风牵挂的事太多了。

但秦琅很快就发现自己错了。

曾经喊着“不关心侵略者背后令人心酸的缘由”的夏兮风，不再把整个“外神世界”当成敌人。

他有了更具体更确切的敌人，并发现自己能做一些可能作用十分微小，但一定会有一点作用的事，便义无反顾地全身心投入进去。

当藏书阁的书突破一千册，夏兮风一直“没想好长什么样，应该是人形吧”的神体变异了——他的精神溢出，如一片光的海洋，无数知识在海洋里游荡，仿佛字迹形成的游鱼。

他不需要旅行，光的海洋便能从世界本源中获取知识，无数字迹游鱼从大海中涌出，你推我攘地上岸，争先恐后地攀爬，英勇无畏地突破世界的限制，奔向系统的“记录技能”。

不需要秦琅的辅助，知识自己整理自己，每日产出新的书籍。

藏书塔有空间扩展法阵，再多的书都塞得下。书籍很快突破万册……十万册……夏兮风清醒的时间越来越少，全神投入整理知识中。

秦琅无法阻止，因为夏兮风这厮是自愿的。

就像秦琅和自我之神打了十年，夏兮风在一旁默默看着，只在秦琅休息的时候与秦琅交流一样，秦琅也不能阻止夏兮风自愿“进步”。他也只能在夏兮风暂时中止技能的时候，与夏兮风短暂恢复“正常日常”。

没有夏兮风的陪伴，秦琅没理由出门旅游。他便和夏兮风一同在塔顶隐居，除非必要，不出现在人前。

夏兮风沉浸在世界本源中的时间越来越长，从最初一两天，增加到一两个月……现在已经半年了。苏醒的时间更是越来越短。

秦琅将自己的神体也放开，与夏兮风的光海交融。夏兮风的思想一有波动，他立刻就知道。

夏兮风最初录书的时候还会很吵，思维很活跃，光芒缠着秦琅的触须，在秦琅脑海里叽叽喳喳说个不停。

他还会嫌弃秦琅的触须黑黝黝不好看，会吓到别人，强烈建议秦琅把精神触须变成水晶那种晶莹剔透流光溢彩模样，这样漂浮在他的精神海的时候就像是漂亮的大水母。

我们外神也是很萌哒！

秦琅当然无视夏兮风的突发奇想。

在这时，秦琅对夏兮风的“晋级”也没什么焦躁情绪。

夏兮风仍旧吵闹，他能一直抱着夏兮风。夏兮风如他曾经想过的那样，不再与他人交流，不会离开他身边，永远只属于他。

可当夏兮风的意识进一步沉入世界本源，传递的话语渐渐少了，秦琅心中逐渐焦躁。

曾经夏兮风沉睡的时候，无论是睡相还是思维，在秦琅看来都是很吵闹的。

现在夏兮风太安静了。

秦琅曾经以为自己会喜欢夏兮风这样的安静。他约束自己对夏兮风的靠近，担心自己因为不愿夏兮风改变，将夏兮风留在最美好的一刻。

如今的夏兮风简直太符合他那时的预想了，甚至夏兮风还没死，还活着，还会回抱着自己，偶尔也能交流。

他却连夏兮风的安静都接受不了？

秦琅难以想象，如果夏兮风永远不再睁眼看着他，永远不再在他耳边叽叽喳喳地吵闹，永远不会主动牵着他的手拉着他乱跑，他真的能忍受？

他曾经担忧的会伤害到夏兮风的行为，现在看来，简直是黑历史笑话。

为了让夏兮风多说几句话，秦琅回到塔顶的时候，都主动把精神触须变成水母了。

Chapter 129: Second Update (Part 1)

Judging solely by its furnishings, the top of the tower was a perfectly ordinary bedroom.

There were desks, bookshelves, wardrobes, and a large bed. The floor had originally been covered in a thick, soft carpet, but now that carpet was subsumed beneath silver waves, making the floor of the room resemble a shimmering silver sea.

Qin Lang carried Xia Xifeng to the desk, upon which lay a thick stack of documents requiring the Headmaster's personal review and approval.

He sat down in the chair to grade and process the paperwork, while Xia Xifeng remained cradled in his arms with his arms wrapped around his neck, slowly closing his eyes as he resumed his deep "slumber."

Slender tentacles trickled out from Qin Lang's shadow, gently surrounding and sheltering Xia Xifeng in his embrace. Even without Qin Lang holding him with his hands, Xia Xifeng could sleep peacefully in his arms.

The silver waves on the floor rippled softly, with shadowy tentacles floating within them. As the tentacles absorbed the silver hue, their original murky color was coated in a layer of silvery brilliance, making them appear semi-transparent and bestowing a mesmerizing, flowing luster upon the deep, lightless tendrils.

The white little beast flew into the top-floor room, and upon seeing the anomalous phenomena inside, its eyes still could not conceal its astonishment.

The black little beast flew up right behind it. "Even though the two of us have accepted Xia and Qin, for them to quietly ignite divine fire in this world is just absurdly impressive."

The white little beast nodded in agreement.

Hearing the voices of the two small creatures, Qin Lang waved the document in his hand behind his back without turning around, signaling the two tiny beasts to carry the finished documents downstairs.

When it came to ordering around divine projections, Qin Lang had never pulled his punches.

The two little beast porters flew over to the desk, extending their short legs to sit down.

The white little beast said worriedly, "Xia has been asleep for so long this time—he hasn't woken up for six months. Six months ago, he only stayed conscious for a few hours. Is he really going to be alright?"

The black little beast cared only about its snacks. "Curse that Xia Xifeng! He hasn't made me any treats for half a year!"

Qin Lang cast a sideways glance at the two fluffballs but offered no reply.

Xia Xifeng was indeed fine for the time being, but Qin Lang was in a terrible mood and refused to consider this state acceptable.

After establishing the academy and updating the system tasks, the localized Appraisal skill loosened the shackles on Qin Lang's body dramatically. His strength soared at an astonishing speed, quickly igniting his divine fire and returning him to the rank of a demigod.

According to the system's original statement, he and Xia Xifeng were unregistered gatecrashers who should not have been able to ignite divine fire in this world, doomed to remain capped at the Legendary realm.

Yet perhaps because the God of Light and the God of Darkness were too deeply entangled with the world, effectively becoming spokespersons for the world's consciousness, They recognized Xia Xifeng and joined forces to shield him from the gaze of the God Emperor. As a result, Xia Xifeng and Qin Lang returned to their rightful realm, becoming the "Outer Gods" of this world.

Thereafter, Xia Xifeng and Qin Lang's strength climbed continuously. Their divine fire grew increasingly potent, their bond with this world deepened, and their power almost matched their former peak in the Dream World.

Xia Xifeng continuously utilized his Appraisal skill to comprehend the affairs of this world, recording knowledge into the system. After Qin Lang organized it, the system compiled the data into books.

During that period, their life was still very normal. Xia Xifeng spent only half a day recording books, while the remaining half was spent farming, crafting, teaching, or letting Qin Lang—who could once again use Shadow Teleportation (a privilege granted by the God of Darkness)—take him traveling all over the world.

This world was still peaceful and had few powerhouses. Qin Lang could take Xia Xifeng roaming across the realm, visiting far more places than they ever had in the Dream World.

Every time they reached a new location, Xia Xifeng would cast Appraisal skill after Appraisal skill, analyzing the valuable ores, flora, and fauna of the region. After Qin Lang categorized and organized the information, the system generated comprehensive compendiums.

After their travels, Xia Xifeng would return to the academy to experiment with crafting items using the newly discovered materials.

Once he mastered the application of these new materials, he had the system transcribe them into books, adding yet another volume to the collection in the Library Tower.

Traveling abroad, returning home to refine compendiums, teasing the students along the way to increase the difficulty of their exams... Initially, Qin Lang thoroughly enjoyed this way of life.

Although this world also faced an impending apocalypse, the calamity was already predestined. Anything done was merely a futile struggle; since the outcome did not matter, every day was spent with ease and tranquility.

Aside from the two fluffballs constantly intruding upon his and Xia Xifeng's private life, Qin Lang was actually somewhat more satisfied with life in this world than in the Dream World.

In the Dream World, there were too many things holding Xia Xifeng's heart.

Yet Qin Lang soon realized he had been mistaken.

Xia Xifeng, who had once declared that he "did not care about the tragic backstories of invaders," no longer viewed the entire "Outer God World" as an enemy.

He now had a more specific, tangible enemy. Upon discovering that he could perform actions that might have a miniscule impact—yet undeniably *some* impact—he cast aside all hesitation and threw himself into it heart and soul.

When the collection of books in the Library Tower surpassed one thousand volumes, Xia Xifeng's divine body—which he had previously said he "hadn't decided on a form for, though it should probably be human"—underwent a mutation. His spiritual essence overflowed like an ocean of light, within which countless pieces of knowledge swam about like fish composed of written script.

He no longer needed to travel; the sea of light could extract knowledge directly from the world's origin. Countless script-fish surged up from the ocean, jostling and scrambling ashore, scaling walls with fearless valor to break through the world's boundaries and rush toward the system's "Record Skill."

Without needing Qin Lang's assistance, the knowledge organized itself, producing new books daily.

The Library Tower possessed spatial expansion arrays, capable of accommodating any number of books. The collection swiftly shattered ten thousand volumes... one hundred thousand volumes... and Xia Xifeng spent less and less time conscious, immersing his entire being into organizing knowledge.

Qin Lang had no way to stop him, for the simple reason that Xia Xifeng was doing this willingly.

Just as Qin Lang had fought the God of Self for ten years while Xia Xifeng watched silently from the side, interacting with him only when he rested, Qin Lang likewise could not stop Xia Xifeng's voluntary "advancement." He could only share brief moments of "normal daily life" with Xia Xifeng during the short intervals when the skill was temporarily paused.

Without Xia Xifeng's companionship, Qin Lang had no reason to travel. He chose to live in seclusion alongside Xia Xifeng at the top of the tower, refusing to appear before others unless absolutely necessary.

The duration Xia Xifeng spent immersed in the world's origin grew longer and longer, stretching from a day or two to a month or two... and now, a full half-year. The windows of his awakening grew ever shorter.

Qin Lang unfurled his own divine body as well, merging it with Xia Xifeng's sea of light. The moment Xia Xifeng experienced any mental ripple, Qin Lang knew instantly.

When Xia Xifeng first began recording books, he was still very noisy and mentally active. His light would entwine with Qin Lang's tentacles, chattering non-stop in Qin Lang's mind.

He would even dislike Qin Lang's tentacles for being dark and gloomy, claiming they would scare people. He strongly urged Qin Lang to transform his mental tentacles into a crystal-clear, radiant appearance like jellyfish, so that floating in his mental sea would look like beautiful big jellyfish.

*We Outer Gods can be super cute too!*

Qin Lang had, of course, ignored Xia Xifeng's sudden whims at the time.

Back then, Qin Lang felt no anxiety regarding Xia Xifeng's "leveling up."

Xia Xifeng was still noisy, and Qin Lang could hold him continuously. Xia Xifeng was just as Qin Lang had once envisioned: no longer interacting with others, never leaving his side, belonging exclusively to him forever.

Yet as Xia Xifeng's consciousness sank deeper into the world's origin, the words he transmitted gradually dwindled, and a growing sense of restlessness took root in Qin Lang's heart.

When Xia Xifeng used to sleep, whether in terms of posture or mental activity, Qin Lang had always found him rather noisy.

Now, Xia Xifeng was far too quiet.

Qin Lang had once believed he would enjoy this quiet side of Xia Xifeng. He used to restrain his urge to draw closer, worried that his unwillingness to see Xia Xifeng change would prompt him to freeze Xia Xifeng forever at his most beautiful moment.

The current Xia Xifeng aligned almost perfectly with his past imagination. Xia Xifeng wasn't dead; he was alive, still hugging him back, and still capable of occasional communication.

Yet he couldn't even endure Xia Xifeng's quietness now?

Qin Lang could hardly imagine: if Xia Xifeng were to never open his eyes to look at him again, never chatter noisily in his ear again, never take the initiative to hold his hand and drag him along on wild runs... could he truly bear it?

The actions he had once worried would harm Xia Xifeng now seemed like nothing more than a laughable piece of dark history.

Just to get Xia Xifeng to say a few more words, Qin Lang had actively transformed his spiritual tentacles into jellyfish upon returning to the top of the tower.

秦琅摸了摸怀里安睡的夏兮风的脸，眉间皱纹又深了几分。

白色小兽见秦琅不回答，知道秦琅心情很不好，心虚地叹了口气，不再问了。

黑色小兽可不会惯着秦琅，祂嘲笑秦琅：“等夏醒来，看见你眉间有皱纹，肯定会惊讶你怎么变老啦！他说不定会嫌弃你变老啦！”

秦琅翻了个白眼，不和已死之神计较。

白色小兽抓住黑色小兽的尾巴，一边用魔法拖运文件，一边把黑色小兽拽走，不让黑色小兽继续挑衅秦琅。

夏兮风正为了这个注定没有未来的世界拼尽全力，小黑还捣乱，太不像话了。

白色小兽和黑色小兽离开后，秦琅抱着夏兮风来到窗边，打开了窗户。

风拂过夏兮风的发丝，夏兮风往秦琅怀里拱了拱。

“来捣乱的人都走了，不会再吵你。”

“再过不久又到了期末考试，你不想个新花样折磨学生？”

“研究粮食育种的魔法师越来越多了，他们看了你的书，自称德鲁伊，即使他们并不知道什么是德鲁伊。”

“各国法师塔都在开设魔导器制作课，有好几座法师塔因为爆炸扰民而迁徙到无人的荒野。或许你该为他们制定安全操作规范。”

“光明神和黑暗神说有属神怀疑我们。祂们说我们是祂们认定可以成神的恩赐者，那群属神都信了。神灵大多都没脑子吗？如梦世界智慧、进化、自我、死亡那样的有脑子的神灵，在这个世界难道不存在？”

“……你还要睡多久？”

夏兮风仍旧在沉睡，一句话都没回应。

以前他总会回应秦琅的每一句话。秦琅说一句话，他能回一大堆话。

秦琅不说话，他自顾自地都能说一大堆话。

“小风，你怎么总是为不相关的人不爱惜自己。我有点生气。”

秦琅垂下视线，看着夏兮风的睡颜。

【哎？没有啊！我只是在晋级变强，才没有不爱惜自己！别胡说，不准生气！】

熟悉的声音通过精神触须，传递到了秦琅耳中。

夏兮风终于回应了。

秦琅轻笑了一声，低头亲了亲夏兮风的额头。

“行，我信你。”

不信还能怎么办？

秦琅反复推翻自己以前所有构想，最后不得不承认，他确实拿夏兮风无可奈何。

从小到大都一样。

……

时间一天一天地过去，夏兮风每次沉睡的时间开始以年为计。

秦琅分了一具分身协助光明神和黑暗神处理学院的事务。夏兮风沉睡的时候，他的本体轻轻拥住夏兮风，不再离开塔顶。

作者有话要说：

补偿的二更到账。明天争取继续加更。

Chapter 129: Second Update (Part 2)

Qin Lang stroked the face of the sleeping Xia Xifeng in his arms, the crease between his brows deepening further.

Seeing that Qin Lang offered no response, the white little beast knew he was in a foul mood. It let out a guilty sigh and ceased asking.

The black little beast, however, would never indulge Qin Lang. It mocked him, "When Xia wakes up and sees wrinkles on your forehead, he'll definitely be shocked by how old you've gotten! He might even start disliking you for growing old!"

Qin Lang rolled his eyes, refusing to lower himself to argue with a deceased deity.

The white little beast grabbed the black little beast's tail, using magic to haul the stack of documents away while dragging the black creature along, preventing it from provoking Qin Lang any further.

Xia Xifeng was currently pouring all his strength into saving this world that was doomed to have no future. For Little Black to cause trouble at a time like this was simply out of line.

After the two little beasts left, Qin Lang carried Xia Xifeng over to the window and pushed it open.

The breeze ruffled Xia Xifeng's strands of hair, and he snuggled deeper into Qin Lang's chest.

"The troublemakers are all gone. No one will disturb you anymore."

"The final exams are approaching again soon. Don't you want to come up with a new trick to torment the students?"

"More and more mages are researching crop breeding. After reading your books, they started calling themselves Druids, even though they have no idea what a Druid actually is."

"Mage towers across various nations are opening courses on magitech crafting. Several of them had to relocate to desolate wilds because their accidental explosions were disturbing the locals. Perhaps you should draft a set of safety operation guidelines for them."

"The God of Light and the God of Darkness said some subordinate gods were harboring suspicions about us. They claimed we were blessed ones They personally deemed worthy of godhood, and those subordinate gods actually fell for it. Are most gods truly so brainless? Do smart gods like Wisdom, Evolution, Self, and Death from the Dream World simply not exist in this realm?"

"...How much longer do you plan to sleep?"

Xia Xifeng remained in a deep slumber, offering not a single word in reply.

In the past, he would always respond to every word Qin Lang said. For every single sentence Qin Lang uttered, he could rattle off a whole barrage in return.

Even if Qin Lang remained silent, he could babble endlessly on his own.

"Xiaofeng, why do you always neglect yourself for people who have nothing to do with you? I'm getting a little angry."

Qin Lang lowered his gaze, looking down at Xia Xifeng's sleeping face.

【*Huh? No I'm not! I'm just leveling up and getting stronger, I'm definitely not neglecting myself! Don't talk nonsense, and you're not allowed to be angry!*】

A familiar voice was transmitted directly into Qin Lang's ears via the spiritual tentacles.

Xia Xifeng had finally responded.

Qin Lang let out a soft laugh, leaning down to kiss Xia Xifeng's forehead.

"Fine. I believe you."

What else could he do except believe him?

Qin Lang had repeatedly overturned all his past assumptions, ultimately forced to admit that he was truly helpless when it came to Xia Xifeng.

It had been this way since childhood.

...

As days turned into weeks, the length of Xia Xifeng's sleep cycles began to be measured in years.

Qin Lang manifested a avatar to assist the God of Light and the God of Darkness in managing the academy's affairs. Meanwhile, whenever Xia Xifeng slept, Qin Lang's true body held him gently in his arms, never again leaving the top of the tower.

***

The compensatory second update has arrived. I will strive to keep adding extra chapters tomorrow!

第130章 一更

在连神灵都不能窥见的世界核心中，银色光海沉沉浮浮，似乎要与世界核心合为一体。

【……我有点生气。】

一声很轻很轻的声音响起，仿佛来自很遥远很遥远的地方。

银色光海剧烈震荡，出现了一个很大的漩涡。光海朝着漩涡收缩，凝聚成一个面目模糊的发光人体。

“啊……咳咳……”人影好像很久没说话，张嘴的时候竟不习惯自己的声音了。

干咳了好几声，他才将双手捧在嘴边做喇叭状，用尽浑身力气大喊道：“哎？没有啊！我只是在晋级变强，才没有不爱惜自己！别胡说，不准生气！”

【行，我信你。】

人影放下双手，面目越来越清晰，光亮越来越微弱。

夏兮风脸上出现庆幸的表情。

还好及时听到了。不然秦琅可太难哄了。

夏兮风揉了揉脸，伸了个大大的懒腰，又做了一套伸展体操。

许久没有恢复人形，他有点不适应自己人形的模样，得习惯习惯。

“唉，你能不能老实点，我不可能和你合为一体的。阿琅还在外面等着我呢。”夏兮风叉着腰，对缩成小球的世界核心道，“老老实实把知识吐出来，别做多余的事。”

小球不甘心地跳了跳，似乎不肯放弃。

夏兮风挠了挠头，很无奈。

破灭世界的残影即使知道自己已经破灭，仍旧想抓住一切机会求生。

当祂觉察到夏兮风来自其他救世主的世界后，就想和夏兮风合为一体，看能不能改变自己既定的命运。

合体不是吞噬，和世界本源合为一体，不会伤害到夏兮风。

夏兮风的实力会暴增。如果世界还活着，他能与天地同寿；如果世界还是死了，他不会和世界同死，还可能得到世界的遗产。

唯一的问题是，与世界本源合体，夏兮风会沉睡很多年才能消化世界规则。

秦琅还在外面等着他呢！

而且与别的东西合体后，夏兮风不确定自己还是不是原本的自己。即使他拥有“夏兮风”的外貌和记忆，可内里加了点别的东西，总感觉自己有一点点不纯粹。

以秦琅情感的纤细程度，夏兮风怀疑秦琅会钻牛角尖。

所以夏兮风感受到了世界本源的善意，也知道与世界本源融合是许多强者梦寐以求的事，不会影响他将来超脱，但他还是十分感动地拒绝了。

生存是所有有生命的存在的最基本的欲/求。哪怕知道希望几乎不存在，世界也想再挣扎一次，所以锲而不舍地向夏兮风展现自己的一切。

世界本源没有强迫夏兮风做什么。夏兮风留在这里，实力就能飞速上升；如果夏兮风在窥伺世界规则的时候一不留神和世界本源同化了，那就是夏兮风自己的选择。

夏兮风是个倔强不服输的人，世界本源敢展露自己，他就敢看。

有人在外面等着自己，他才不会和世界本源同化呢。

“我劝你放弃吧，别白费力气，不如积攒起来给你的创世神一记狠的。”夏兮风坐在小球旁边，“或许对经历了无数年，诞生了无数生灵的你而言，不能理解两个渺小的人类之间的感情。但我们人类的心就是这么小。”

好不容易恢复了人形，话痨夏兮风赶紧多说点话，絮絮叨叨和世界本源说起自己和秦琅的过去。

所有人都说他对秦琅很偏爱，但夏兮风逐渐理清自己的心后，明白他对秦琅的“偏爱”，来自秦琅对他的“偏爱”。

“阿琅老说他离精神病只有一线，与普通人思想不同。”夏兮风笑了笑，道，“我不也一样？”

什么救世主性格，虽然是正面的“与众不同”，不也是与众不同吗？

夏兮风一直都知道自己与众不同。

小时候不清楚，等他长大了，看了很多书，接触了很多人，他哪能不清楚自己老想做好事，还不计较回报的性格怪怪的。

做好事的人很多，做好事不求回报的人很多，但不求回报不代表别人的回应是恩将仇报的时候，心里不会难过。

只要是个正常人，被夸奖了会开心自豪，被伤害了会难过愤怒，这才是人之常情。

夏兮风却不是这样。

做好事是他的爱好，他不仅不在意回报，也不在意别人的回应。

这真的很奇怪。

虽然奇怪，但他是个好人，一个在大众眼中品德高尚的人，所以虽然有人担忧他的安全，只要他做好万全的准备，别人不会禁止他做好事。

只有秦琅，会让他自私些。

万全的准备也不是万无一失，做好事不求回报只会让别人得寸进尺。哪怕他只要被“背叛”一次就不会对那个人再伸出援手，但许多夏兮风做的好事都是针对陌生人，陌生人也不需要再让夏兮风伸出一次援手，这根本不算威慑。

“对阿琅而言，我才是最重要的。”夏兮风不好意思地揉了揉鼻子，颇为骄傲道，“就算我不是个好人也没关系！他还更高兴呢！”

世界本源如果能模拟出露水，一定会给自己的小球笼罩上雾水。

真是满头雾水啊，你究竟骄傲个什么啊！

夏兮风知道别人不能理解，正如他不在乎别人对他做好事的回应一样，他也不在意别人是否理解。

他只是想说而已。

“虽然穿越是一件好事，但一想到我差点连累阿琅陪我一起死，我就后悔了。”夏兮风笑容淡去，“我第一次后悔，为什么要去见义勇为。”

“所以你别再尝试了，我是不可能与世界本源融合的。即使你再说多少次不会有危险，但我不会再冒未知的危险。”夏兮风认真道，“因为我出事，阿琅会跟着我出事。我想帮助这个世界，前提是不伤害到阿琅。”

天生的救世主也是人，如果救世行为会伤害到自己重要的人，他也不想当这个救世主。

而重要的人的安危在于自己的安危，自己必须活着重要的人才会幸福，那他就必须爱惜自己胜过爱世。

“赶紧干活，早点干完活，我早点回去。”夏兮风笑眯眯地拍了拍世界球球，“阿琅还在等着我呢。唉，往外面递消息越来越费劲，我都寂寞了。”

世界球球抖了抖，似乎被夏兮风的自我剖析雷得不轻。

夏兮风：“不然，你把阿琅也叫来？他也能用抄写技能，让他帮我一起抄写知识，效率更高。”

世界球球又抖了抖。

祂不放秦琅进来，就是知道秦琅的“自我”太强大，绝对不可能和祂融合，所以祂才不费这个力气。

而夏兮风是天生的救世主，救世主的“自我”都是很薄弱的。

真不知道谁设置的“护道者”配置。谁会专门培养救世主的自私之心啊？！

不过……

稚嫩的世界意识看着夏兮风的双眼。

夏兮风眼中满是对未来美好生活的希望。有希望，这样的救世主会很难死吧？

世界不需要担心救世主会放弃救世，祂们只担心救世主奋不顾身，太容易死了。

所以“护道者”是必须的。

Chapter 130: First Update

In the core of the world, a place invisible even to the gods, a sea of silver light ebbed and flowed, seemingly on the verge of merging with the world's very heart.

【...I am a little angry.】

A voice, faint and ethereal, echoed as if from a place infinitely far away.

The silver sea of light trembled violently, forming a massive vortex. The light contracted toward the center, coalescing into a glowing, featureless human form.

"Ah... cough, cough..." The figure seemed unaccustomed to speaking, as if it had been silent for an eternity.

After a few dry coughs, he cupped his hands around his mouth like a megaphone and shouted with all his might: "Hey? No, I'm not! I'm just leveling up and getting stronger; I haven't been neglecting myself! Don't talk nonsense, and you are not allowed to be angry!"

【Fine, I believe you.】

The figure lowered his hands. His features became increasingly distinct, while the radiance grew dim.

A look of relief washed over Xia Xifeng’s face.

It was a good thing he’d heard that in time. Otherwise, Qin Lang would have been far too difficult to coax.

Xia Xifeng rubbed his face, stretched his arms wide, and went through a set of stretching exercises.

Having not returned to human form for so long, he felt a bit awkward in his own skin; he needed to get used to it again.

"Sigh, can you just be honest? I cannot merge with you. A-Lang is still waiting for me outside," Xia Xifeng said, hands on his hips, addressing the world core that had shrunk into a small ball. "Just spit out the knowledge obediently and stop trying to pull any tricks."

The little ball hopped about resentfully, seemingly unwilling to give up.

Xia Xifeng scratched his head, feeling helpless.

Even though the remnant of this ruined world knew it had already perished, it still clung to every opportunity to survive.

Once it realized that Xia Xifeng came from the world of another Savior, it had tried to merge with him, hoping to alter its predetermined fate.

Merging was not the same as being devoured. Becoming one with the world's origin would not harm Xia Xifeng.

In fact, Xia Xifeng’s strength would skyrocket. If the world were still alive, he could live as long as heaven and earth; even if the world remained dead, he would not die with it and might even inherit the world's legacy.

The only problem was that merging with the world's origin would force Xia Xifeng into a deep slumber for many years while he digested the world's rules.

But Qin Lang was still waiting for him outside!

Furthermore, after merging with something else, Xia Xifeng wasn't sure if he would still be himself. Even if he possessed the appearance and memories of "Xia Xifeng," if his inner self had been tainted by something else, he would feel a lack of purity.

Given the delicate nature of Qin Lang's emotions, Xia Xifeng suspected that Qin Lang would spiral into despair.

Thus, although Xia Xifeng felt the goodwill of the world's origin and knew that merging was something many powerhouses dreamed of—and that it wouldn't hinder his future transcendence—he still refused, albeit with deep gratitude.

Survival is the most basic desire of all living things. Even knowing that hope was almost non-existent, the world wanted to struggle one last time, so it persistently displayed everything it had to Xia Xifeng.

The world's origin did not force Xia Xifeng to do anything. If Xia Xifeng stayed here, his strength would rise rapidly; if he accidentally assimilated with the world's origin while peering into its rules, that would be his own choice.

Xia Xifeng was a stubborn person who refused to admit defeat. If the world's origin dared to reveal itself, he dared to look.

But with someone waiting for him outside, he would never assimilate with the world's origin.

"I advise you to give up. Don't waste your effort; you'd be better off saving it to land a heavy blow on your Creator," Xia Xifeng said, sitting down beside the little ball. "Perhaps for you, having existed for countless years and birthed countless lives, you cannot understand the feelings between two tiny humans. But our human hearts are just this small."

Having finally regained his human form, the chatterbox Xia Xifeng hurried to speak, rambling on to the world's origin about his past with Qin Lang.

Everyone said he was biased toward Qin Lang, but after Xia Xifeng gradually sorted out his own heart, he realized that his "bias" toward Qin Lang stemmed from Qin Lang's "bias" toward him.

"A-Lang always says he’s only a hair's breadth away from being a psychopath, and that his way of thinking is different from ordinary people," Xia Xifeng smiled and said. "Aren't I the same?"

What kind of "Savior" personality was that? Even if it was a positive "difference," wasn't it still a difference?

Xia Xifeng had always known he was different.

He didn't realize it when he was a child, but as he grew up, read many books, and met many people, how could he not see that his personality—always wanting to do good deeds without caring about the returns—was strange?

There are many people who do good deeds, and many who do them without seeking reward. But not seeking reward doesn't mean one wouldn't feel sad when the response is betrayal.

It is human nature for a normal person to feel happy and proud when praised, and sad and angry when hurt.

But Xia Xifeng was not like that.

Doing good was his hobby. He didn't care about the returns, nor did he care about how others responded.

It was truly strange.

Although strange, he was a good person, someone viewed by the public as having noble character. So, while some worried about his safety, as long as he made thorough preparations, no one would stop him from doing good.

Only Qin Lang would urge him to be a bit more selfish.

Thorough preparation was not foolproof, and doing good without seeking reward only made others push their luck. Even if he vowed never to help someone again after being "betrayed" once, many of the good deeds Xia Xifeng did were for strangers. Strangers didn't need him to help them a second time, so that wasn't a deterrent.

"To A-Lang, I am the most important thing," Xia Xifeng said, rubbing his nose in embarrassment, looking quite proud. "Even if I weren't a good person, it wouldn't matter! He’d be even happier!"

If the world's origin could simulate dew, it would surely have shrouded its little ball in mist.

What a fog of confusion—what exactly are you so proud of?!

Xia Xifeng knew others couldn't understand. Just as he didn't care about others' responses to his good deeds, he didn't care if they understood him.

He just wanted to say it.

"Although transmigrating was a good thing, the moment I thought I almost dragged A-Lang to his death with me, I regretted it," Xia Xifeng's smile faded. "It was the first time I regretted being a Good Samaritan."

"So, don't try again. It is impossible for me to merge with the world's origin. No matter how many times you say there is no danger, I will not take unknown risks," Xia Xifeng said earnestly. "Because if something happens to me, A-Lang will suffer too. I want to help this world, but the prerequisite is not hurting A-Lang."

A natural-born Savior is still a human. If saving the world would hurt the people important to him, he wouldn't want to be that Savior.

And since the safety of his loved ones depended on his own, he had to stay alive for them to be happy. Therefore, he had to cherish himself more than he cherished the world.

"Hurry up and get to work. The sooner we finish, the sooner I can go back," Xia Xifeng said, patting the world-ball with a smile. "A-Lang is still waiting for me. Sigh, it's getting harder and harder to send messages outside; I'm so lonely."

The world-ball shivered, seemingly struck by Xia Xifeng’s self-analysis.

Xia Xifeng: "Otherwise, why don't you bring A-Lang in too? He can also use the copying skill. Let him help me copy the knowledge; it would be more efficient."

The world-ball shivered again.

The reason it didn't let Qin Lang in was that it knew Qin Lang's "self" was too powerful; it was absolutely impossible to merge with him, so it didn't bother wasting the effort.

But Xia Xifeng was a natural-born Savior, and a Savior's "self" is always very fragile.

He really didn't know who had set up the "Guardian" configuration. Who would specifically cultivate a Savior's selfishness?!

However...

The nascent world consciousness looked into Xia Xifeng’s eyes.

In those eyes, there was nothing but hope for a beautiful future. With hope, such a Savior would be hard to kill, right?

The world didn't need to worry about the Savior giving up on saving it; it only worried about the Savior being too reckless and dying too easily.

That was why a "Guardian" was necessary.

他们护的不仅是先知的身，更是先知的心。有“护道者”这个锚点，先知才会重视自身，无数次从危险中归来。

而且只有重视自身，才会有“自我”。夏兮风只是夏兮风，不是什么被救世主性格异化的符号。他也有与拯救世界无关的自私梦想，比如和秦琅永远不分离，如他自记事起一样。

只有秦琅想要离开的时候，夏兮风会无数次地奔向秦琅，把秦琅的手牢牢抓住，不准秦琅离开。

不过……嗯，夏兮风回忆过往，虽然秦琅无数次嘴上说着要离开，行为上好像没离开过？

就是大学分离了两年，但他们每天还一起打游戏呢，日常都没断过。这算哪门子的分离？

夏兮风又沉浸在和秦琅的回忆中了。

世界小球瘪了瘪，像是叹了口气。

空间震荡，出现一个小小的洞口。

一朵“水母”滑了进来。

夏兮风眼睛一亮，扑了上去，将自己埋在了水母中：“阿琅！你还真变成水母了！”

水母瞬间变色，重新变回灰黑色。

夏兮风在触须中笑得打滚，嘲笑秦琅死要面子。

触须把夏兮风抓起来放好，然后变成了人形的模样。

秦琅揽住挂在他脖子上嘲笑他的夏兮风，双眼如刀子般剜向世界小球：“恩将仇报的东西，杀了吧。”

“哈哈哈哈，和世界本源融合不算恩将仇报吧？”夏兮风笑得趴在秦琅怀里起不来，“再说了，祂本来就是死的。”

秦琅嘴角抽搐了一下。

“人”死为大。算了，不和已死的世界计较。

“好多知识，根本抄不完，来帮我！”夏兮风嚷嚷。

秦琅：“嗯。”

他分出一个分身干杂活，本体和夏兮风一起睡了。

夏兮风睡多久，他就睡多久。

夏兮风的神体又变成了光的海洋，灰黑色的触须在海洋中沉沉浮浮。每一滴海水中，都有细小的触须游荡。

世界本源小球缩了缩。

咦！原本神圣的光之海洋中全是脏东西！

【阿琅啊，我说真的，你还是变成水晶丝触须吧。你这样好像我的水体被污染了。】

【水体污染？！】

世界本源小球上下晃动，疑似点头。

【我实话实说你怎么还生气啦？唉，你这人真小气，我说实话你都要生气。心胸好狭隘啊。】

【闭嘴。干活。】

【好久没和你说话了，我就要说，我就要说。】

【。】

【要不，我给你唱首歌吧！】

【……】

秦琅实在是不堪其扰，无奈褪色。

他怀疑，世界诞生夏兮风，就是为了气死他:）。

作者有话要说：

上一章的小风视角。我说了小情侣一直甜甜蜜蜜锁死。秦琅跟着睡了是因为夏兮风把他拉过去了，一起干活呢，不是啥寂寞地自闭哈哈哈哈。

昨天熬太晚了，有点头疼，明天再补加更。
chunks.englishText:
Chapter 130: First Update (Part 2)

They guarded not only the Prophet's body but also the Prophet's heart. With the "Guardian" as an anchor, the Prophet would value their own life and return from danger time and time again.

Moreover, only by valuing oneself could one possess a "self." Xia Xifeng was just Xia Xifeng, not some symbol alienated by the Savior personality. He also had selfish dreams unrelated to saving the world, such as never being separated from Qin Lang, just as it had been since he could remember.

Only when Qin Lang wanted to leave would Xia Xifeng rush toward him countless times, grabbing his hand firmly and refusing to let him go.

However... hmm, Xia Xifeng recalled the past. Although Qin Lang had said he wanted to leave countless times, he didn't seem to have ever actually left in his actions.

They had been separated for two years during college, but they still played games together every day; their daily routine had never been broken. What kind of separation was that?

Xia Xifeng was once again immersed in memories of Qin Lang.

The little world-ball deflated, as if sighing.

Space rippled, and a small hole appeared.

A "jellyfish" slid in.

Xia Xifeng’s eyes lit up, and he pounced, burying himself in the jellyfish: "A-Lang! You really turned into a jellyfish!"

The jellyfish changed color instantly, reverting to a grayish-black.

Xia Xifeng rolled around laughing in the tentacles, mocking Qin Lang for being so concerned about his image.

The tentacles picked Xia Xifeng up, set him down, and then transformed into a human shape.

Qin Lang embraced Xia Xifeng, who was hanging around his neck and mocking him, his eyes cutting toward the little world-ball like knives: "Ungrateful thing, let's kill it."

"Hahahaha, merging with the world's origin doesn't count as being ungrateful, does it?" Xia Xifeng laughed so hard he couldn't get up from Qin Lang's arms. "Besides, it's already dead."

Qin Lang’s mouth twitched.

"The dead are the greatest." Forget it, he wouldn't argue with a dead world.

"So much knowledge, I can't finish copying it at all. Come help me!" Xia Xifeng shouted.

Qin Lang: "Mm."

He split off a clone to do the chores, while his main body slept with Xia Xifeng.

He would sleep as long as Xia Xifeng slept.

Xia Xifeng’s divine body turned back into an ocean of light, with grayish-black tentacles floating within it. In every drop of seawater, tiny tentacles swam about.

The world's origin ball shrank.

Eww! The originally sacred ocean of light was full of dirty things!

【A-Lang, I’m serious, you should turn back into crystal silk tentacles. You look like my water body has been polluted.】

【Water pollution?!】

The world's origin ball wobbled up and down, seemingly nodding.

【Why are you still angry when I'm just telling the truth? Sigh, you're so petty. You get angry even when I speak the truth. How narrow-minded.】

【Shut up. Get to work.】

【I haven't talked to you in so long, I want to talk, I want to talk.】

【.】

【How about I sing you a song!】

【...】

Qin Lang was truly unable to bear the harassment and helplessly faded away.

He suspected that the world had birthed Xia Xifeng just to annoy him to death : ).

Author's Note:
This is the perspective of Little Feng from the previous chapter. I said the couple is always sweet and locked together. Qin Lang slept because Xia Xifeng pulled him over to work together, not because he was lonely or self-isolating, haha.

I stayed up too late yesterday and have a headache, so I'll add an extra update tomorrow.
